newsitem.title: USA: US said to withdraw bid to ship plutonium to Canada.
newsitem.headline: US said to withdraw bid to ship plutonium to Canada.

text.p: The United States has withdrawn its application for a license to ship U.S. military plutonium to Canada to test its use in civilian nuclear reactors, three anti-nuclear groups said on Wednesday.

The groups, which had filed a petition with the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission to block the exports, said they had been notified on Nov. 4 by the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) that it had decided to withdraw the license application.
No comment was immediately available from DOE.

The Nuclear Control Institute, Natural Resources Defense Council, and Greenpeace, had argued that the export of the bomb material as civilan fuel would harm national security and influence a current federal review of options for disposing of surplus plutonium from the U.S. nuclear arsenal.

The pending license application was for the export of slightly more than 2 pounds (1 kilogram) of plutonium contained in fuel pellets to a test reactor at Atomic Energy of Canada Ltd.'s Chalk River Laboratories in Canada.
The groups said eventually as much as 50 tons of surplus weapons-grade plutonium could be made available for the Canadian civil reactor program.
